coverage_of_risk.rationale: No tests exist at all, and the absence concentrates on precisely the riskiest logic: index construction, URL state, and move-table assembly. The pure helpers in format.ts are free wins that were also skipped.

findings.issue: No test script, no test runner, and zero test files for 13 source files containing ~470 LOC of data-shaping logic; the app is guarded only by the external acceptance suite.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest plus a `test` script; start with unit tests for format.ts, home filtering/pagination, and the pokemon loader (via createRoutesStub or direct loader invocation with a stubbed fetch).

findings.issue: The riskiest unit (buildIndex: species→generation map, type aggregation, alternate-form exclusion, dex sort) is entangled with real fetch and module-level memoized promises, so it cannot be unit-tested without a refactor.
findings.suggestion: Extract pure functions that transform already-fetched documents (generation list, type records, species list) into the PokedexIndex, and test them with fixtures.

findings.issue: Search box state is initialised from the URL exactly once; browser back/forward changes type/generation/page but leaves q stale, so rendered results desync from the URL — and no test pins the URL-state round-trip.
findings.suggestion: Derive q from searchParams (or sync it in an effect), and add a test that navigates back/forward and asserts the input, filters and rendered list match the URL.

findings.issue: Move-table assembly — the `move|method` dedup keeping minimum level, default game selection via vgs[length-1], and fixed-then-alphabetical method ordering — is untested; a refactor can drop rows or pick the wrong default game and nothing fails.
findings.suggestion: Extract the per-version-group row/method assembly into a pure function over pokemon.moves and test it against fixture data (multi-method moves, multiple games, missing power/accuracy).

findings.issue: ErrorBoundary renders 'Not found' for every thrown error, so API 500s and network failures (rethrown at pokemon.tsx:60-64 and pokeapi.server.ts:28-32) are masked as 404s; no error-path test exists.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish not-found (loader returns status 404 data) from thrown errors in the boundary, and add a test that simulates an API failure and asserts an error (not not-found) response.

findings.issue: Page clamping can render 'Page 5 of 5' while the URL still says page=22 after filters shrink the result set; untested and a spec-visible mismatch.
findings.suggestion: Replace the clamped page in the URL (or redirect) when it exceeds totalPages, and test the shrinking-filter scenario.

findings.issue: pokemonRefsToCards (alternate-form exclusion via speciesById, duplicate collapse, hidden-ability OR) is untested; wrong output silently corrupts move/ability/type card lists.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test with refs including ids ≥10000, duplicates with differing is_hidden, and refs missing a species entry.

findings.issue: Client-side sorting (nulls-last in both directions, numeric vs localeCompare) is only pinned for two columns of one table by the acceptance suite.
findings.suggestion: Extract the comparator into a pure function and test ascending/descending with mixed nulls on numeric and string columns.

findings.issue: Pure helpers encoding spec rules (humanize, latestEnglishFlavor whitespace collapse, dexNumber padding, englishName fallback) have no tests despite being the cheapest coverage in the repo.
findings.suggestion: Add a small table-driven unit test covering mr-mime, multi-line flavor text, and id padding.

summary: The app ships with zero tests of its own: no runner, no script, no files. Its riskiest logic — index construction, home-page URL state, move-table assembly, error handling — is guarded only by an external acceptance suite the owning team won't maintain, and one real bug (back/forward desync of the search box at home.tsx:35) is already hiding in the untested area. The code is unusually testable (pure helpers, isolated sort logic), so adding a vitest suite over format.ts, extracted index/move-table functions, and the loaders with stubbed fetch would be my merge condition.
